title: Audit evidence event-forwarder: region-tagging, retention enforcement, and DLQ strategy
creator: Elena Martinez
description: Goal: Build an Event Forwarder service (efwd) that reliably ships audit-grade evidence to downstream systems and external partners while preserving data residency assertions and enforcing retention TTLs. Scope includes: the event schema v2 for evidence packages (chronicle manifest), region tagging and residency assertion fields, retention-policy enforcement at delivery time, at-least-once delivery with idempotency, dead-letter queue (DLQ) handling for non-retriable failures, signed evidence bundles for downstream verification, and observability (per-event metrics and delivery traces). This ticket covers the API contract, schema, delivery semantics, DLQ policy, and implementation plan for the efwd microservice prototype.
acceptance_criteria: Publish event schema v2 in Confluence and JSON Schema registry; schema includes region_tag, residency_assertion, retention_ttl_seconds, evidence_manifest_id, and signer_metadata
efwd exposes a POST /v1/evidence-events endpoint with documented idempotency-key header and returns canonical 202 + location for async delivery
Events are routed to region-anchored sinks according to region_tag; delivery attempts respect retention_ttl_seconds and will not forward evidence to a region that violates residency assertions
Non-retriable failures are moved to a durable DLQ (SQS/SNS or internal chronicle-dlq) with failure reason and original envelope; autofixable errors generate follow-up tasks in the console
Integration tests cover happy path, transient failure retry, DLQ insertion, and idempotent replay (same idempotency-key results in single delivered artifact)
implementation_plan: Design: finalise event schema v2 and residency assertion enumerations (confluence: /docs/efwd-schema)
Prototype efwd: lightweight Go service that validates schema, signs a chronicle manifest, and enqueues to region-specific delivery workers
Delivery workers: per-region goroutine pools with exponential backoff, jitter, and circuit-breaker; use KMS-signed HMAC for evidence signing
DLQ: implement durable DLQ store with retention and automated reprocessing CLI to inspect and requeue artifacts
Metrics & tracing: add delivery_latency_ms, delivery_attempts, dlq_inserts, residency_mismatch_count; hook to console dashboards
QA & rollout: run in staging with mirror traffic, then gradual rollout to prod with canary percent and monitoring alerts
notes: 2025-11-18 Elena Martinez: Initial RFC drafted. Chose 'chronicle manifest' naming to differentiate from existing 'evidence' artifacts. Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/COMPLIANCE/Efwd+Schema+v2
2025-11-24 Sanjay Rao: Spike completed for idempotency store using Redis vs Dynamo; opted for Dynamo global table for cross-region durability after latency tests
2025-11-27 Aisha Khan (security): Recommended signed manifests using customer KMS envelope keys for partner verification. Added signer_metadata field to schema
2025-11-30 Engineering: Prototype efwd service created in repo github.com/redwood/efwd (PR: https://github.com/redwood/efwd/pull/42). Basic validation + signing implemented
2025-12-02 Sanjay Rao: Integration test harness for DLQ behavior added (PR: https://github.com/redwood/efwd/pull/57). Tests simulate residency mismatch and expect DLQ insertion with metadata
risks: Residency enforcement complexity: some downstream partners lack region-specific endpoints, requiring data transformation or holding in region-anchored staging
At-least-once semantics increase risk of duplicate evidence unless idempotency is rock-solid; duplicates can cause billing/contract disputes
KMS signing across regions introduces key access latency; need caching and fallback signing keys
DLQ growth if downstream systems misbehave could cause storage and visibility issues; require retention caps and alerting
qa_plan: Unit tests: schema validation, signer logic, idempotency checks
Integration tests: full delivery flow to mock sinks in eu-west-1 and us-east-1, simulate transient network failures
Chaos test: kill delivery worker mid-delivery to validate retry and manifest re-signing behavior
Post-rollout smoke: monitor delivery_latency_ms and dlq_inserts for 48 hours after canary expansion
